name: Movses Xorenac'i
critical_date: disputed; many scholars place composition later
patronage: dedicated to Sahak Bagratuni in the work's own presentation
known_bias_notes: Modern criticism documents systematic glorification of Bagratuni, downgrading of Mamikonean, substitutions of Bagratuni/other figures for Mamikonean protagonists, and chronological distortions.
evidence_policy: Explicit kinship in this source is not high-confidence solely because explicit; must carry disputed-date and patronage flags.

name: Lazar P'arpec'i
work: History of Armenia; Letter to Vahan Mamikonean
patronage: commissioned by Vahan Mamikonean; author raised in Mamikonean household
known_bias_notes: The History is explicitly characterized as an encomium to the Mamikonean family.
evidence_policy: Strong for explicit local kinship/events, but positive Mamikonean narrative centrality must be normalized for patronage.

name: P'awstos Buzand / Epic Histories
claimed_date: traditionally 5th c. Armenian composition drawing on earlier traditions
critical_date: late 5th c. arrangement; fourth-century subject matter
known_bias_notes: Narrative casts heroic Mamikonean sparapets, Arsacid kings and Grigorid patriarchs into epic/hagiographic structures; may preserve a lost Mamikonean geste.
evidence_policy: Do not treat narrative heroism or centrality as neutral evidence of institutional importance; explicit relations remain usable with genre/temporal flags.

name: Elise / Ełise
work: History of Vardan and the Armenian War
claimed_date: traditional 5th c.; dating/history of composition debated
known_bias_notes: Carefully constructed work focused on motivation and martyrdom, influenced by Syriac acts of martyrs; Vardan Mamikonean is central leader/martyr.
evidence_policy: Religious/martyr prestige and narrative centrality are not proxies for political centrality; explicit prosopographic statements require source-profile flags.

name: Anonymous History traditionally attributed to Sebeos
work: Chronological/Royal History traditionally called History of Sebeos
critical_date: 7th c.; attribution to Sebeos rejected by modern scholarship
genre: chronicle/royal history with embedded source blocks

house_affinity.Bagratuni: localized strong positive block around Smbat

known_bias_notes: Contains/uses a laudatory biography of Smbat Bagratuni, but the author also shows broad geopolitical scope and efforts toward neutrality; Smbat is independently corroborated by seal and letters.
evidence_policy: Separate Smbat-biography-derived claims from independently corroborated claims; do not downweight the entire work globally.

name: T'ovma Artsruni / Thomas Artsruni
work: History of the House of the Artsrunik'
critical_date: composition begun under Grigor Derenik and continued under/for Gagik
temporal_distance: contemporary for late 9th c.; highly retrospective for antiquity
patronage: commissioned by Artsruni princes; dedicated to Artsruni house
known_bias_notes: Purpose explicitly includes giving the Artsruni a pedigree and glorious antiquity comparable to rival houses; remote genealogy is programmatic dynastic legitimation.
evidence_policy: Contemporary Artsruni events may be strong; remote ancestry is claims_descent_from unless independently corroborated.
